submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on the descriptive core of a determiner-led noun phrase that introduces or evaluates a referent, typically the attributive adjective (a warm slice, some great stories, the following ways) or the head noun / determiner itself when the phrase has no adjective (the highlight, take a look), with activation ramping from the determiner to the peak token. Breaking the determiner-modifier-head structure, by swapping the determiner, reordering the words, or moving the same word to a predicative or non-adjectival use, collapses the peak even when lexical items are held fixed.

After traveling three billion miles over the course of almost a decade, the New Horizons spacecraft will finally make it to Pluto on July 14, 2015.
"It's Bastille Day," Alan Stern, principal investigator for NASA's Pluto-Kuiper Belt Mission, told NPR. "To celebrate, we're storming the gates of Pluto." New Horizons isn't actually going to land on Pluto, but will fly within 6,000 miles of the dwarf planet. The mission has been calculated so the spacecraft — which is unmanned and the size and shape of a baby grand piano — doesn't get caught in Pluto's orbit, but can still get close enough to take photographs that are not too blurry.
The closest any spacecraft has been to Pluto is one billion miles, and the best images have come from the Hubble Telescope.
